title: A Thermodynamic Pinning Criterion for Two-Dimensional Structural Superlubricity
abstract: Incommensurability and elastic reconstruction do not by themselves define a structurally superlubric phase. We define fully sliding and pinned zero-temperature phases by $\limsup_{A\to\infty}τ_{\rm dep}^{\max}(A)=0$ and $\liminf_{A\to\infty}τ_{\rm dep}^{\min}(A)>0$, respectively; $Λ_n=|V_n|G_{n,i}[D_{\rm rel}^{-1}(\mathbf q_n)]_{ij}G_{n,j}$ measures only reconstruction susceptibility. Translational covariance then proves that a clean, smooth, infinite moiré continuum can reconstruct without acquiring a bulk sliding barrier. We restore atomic sampling in a two-dimensional discrete model of graphene/hBN and test both a diffusion quantum Monte Carlo first-star potential and a 15-harmonic Leven potential across three rational approximants and five directions. No physical-coupling equilibrium or metastable barrier is resolved. The Leven spectrum raises the largest tested $Λ$ from $0.142$ to $0.212$, while artificial scaling through $Λ=1$ reaches uncontrolled strain before a size-independent threshold appears. The tested zero-temperature in-plane models are therefore consistent with an elastically relaxed sliding regime; $Λ=1$ is a reconstruction scale, not a static phase criterion.
summary: This work develops a rigorous thermodynamic framework to define structural superlubricity by analyzing the limits of directional depinning stress at crystalline interfaces like graphene/hBN. The authors demonstrate that simple elastic reconstruction susceptibility ($\Lambda$) is insufficient to predict static pinning, concluding that under ideal conditions, the system remains in an elastically relaxed sliding regime.
main_problem: The authors aim to establish a rigorous thermodynamic criterion for structural superlubricity—the suppression of static friction—at two-dimensional crystalline interfaces.
main_result: The analysis shows that smooth, clean moiré continua cannot generate an extensive bulk sliding barrier; the results are consistent with an elastically relaxed sliding regime rather than a statically pinned phase.
method: They define superlubricity using limits of directional depinning stresses ($	au_{	ext{dep}}$) and distinguish this thermodynamic criterion from reconstruction susceptibility ($\Lambda_n$).
model_or_system: The study uses a two-dimensional discrete model, specifically examining the graphene/hBN interface, governed by an energy functional incorporating elastic terms and generalized stacking-fault energies.
key_observables: Directional depinning stress ($	au_{	ext{dep}}$), equilibrium restoring stress ($\Phi_R$), and reconstruction susceptibility ($\Lambda_n$).
important_parameters: The thermodynamic limits $A	o\infty$ are crucial for defining the true phase; $\Lambda=1$ is identified as a reconstruction scale, not a static phase criterion.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on taking the limit of large contact areas ($A	o\infty$) and assumes zero-temperature, defect-free, in-plane conditions for the primary conclusions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of reconstruction susceptibility ($\Lambda$) on twist angle and show finite-size flow of corrugation, demonstrating that small approximants do not predict large-scale behavior.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the thermodynamic criteria using depinning stresses. It then analyzes continuum models to show that smooth reconstruction is insufficient for pinning. Finally, it applies these rigorous criteria to atomistic simulations (graphene/hBN) to test for resolved static barriers.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state friction, the methodology of defining phase transitions via thermodynamic limits ($\lim_{A	o\infty}$) and distinguishing between different types of order parameters (e.g., susceptibility vs. true barrier height) is highly relevant to understanding phase boundaries in open quantum systems or complex many-body dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Logical structure of the criterion. Bare geometry and elasticity determine the reconstruction susceptibility Λ, whereas the thermodynamic phase is determined by the size scaling of the depinning stress τdep; ΦR and τeq diagnose its equilibrium corrugation. Reconstruction is not sufficient for bulk static pinning. Exact commensuration can produce a bulk barrier, while edges and defects can pin finite contacts.
